## 0) Corrections (anti-flattery: includes my errors and those from July 2)

The independent audit **overturned two claims that I had previously given you as strong**. I explicitly correct them:

1. **"The steer gets stuck on the line because case 7 does not call `serialEvent5()`."** → **FALSE.** On Teensy 4.x the `Wire` (I2C) library calls `yield()` while waiting for each transfer (confirmed in authoritative PJRC source). The line loop makes I2C readings **every iteration** (`leer_tof()` → 2× VL53L0X, `ajustarVelocidadPorPendiente()` → BNO055, `get_color_fast()` → APDS9960), and each one triggers `yield()` → which executes `serialEvent5()`. **The serial IS drained several times per loop; `steer`/`green_state`/`silver_line` are fresh.** This also refutes the item "serial not drained on line" from July 2. (Reconciles with what was observed: that’s why the robot did follow curves and reacted to the greens.)

2. **"The pitch is read from the wrong axis (`.y` = roll)."** → **NOT VERIFIABLE BY CODE; it is a documented contradiction.** Authoritative sources contradict each other: the Bosch datasheet + the order of Euler registers say `.y = roll, .z = pitch`; but the **Adafruit vendorized examples in the repo itself** (`test/sensors/BNO055_examples/webserial3d.cpp:112`, `bunny.cpp:100-104`) label `.y = pitch, .z = roll`. Since the effective axis also depends on the **physical mounting** of the chip, this **can only be resolved by measuring** (see P1, Step 0). I withdraw my previous claim that `.y` was surely roll.

Both corrections are why this audit was worthwhile: two previous "certainties" did not survive independent verification.

## 1) The technical fact that reorders EVERYTHING (VERIFIED-IN-CODE)

**The firmware already delivers maximum PWM (255) to the wheel when it brakes. There is no "more force" to give by software.**

Verified chain from zero:
- The motors use **pure speed PID, integral only**: `drivebase.h:30` `_kp=0, _ki=22, _kd=0`. The "speed" of `robot.steer()` is **setpoint of RPM**, not PWM (`drivebase.cpp:113`, `drivebase.h:16 setSpeed(int dir, double rpm)`).
- With kp=kd=0 the output IS the integrator (`PID.cpp:64` `outputSum += ki*error`; `PID.cpp:85/91` `output = outputSum`), saturated to **[0, 255]** (`PID.cpp:22`).
- Internal `ki` = `22 × 0.1 = 2.2` per 100 ms cycle (`PID.cpp:127`, `SampleTime=100`).
- **`PID::Reset()` is never called** (0 matches in the firmware) → the integrator accumulates freely.
- If the wheel brakes on the ramp, `error ≈ 40 RPM` → `outputSum` rises ~`2.2×40 = 88`/cycle → **saturates to 255 in ~3 cycles (~300 ms)**. `analogWrite(pin, 255 - _pwmVal)` (`drivebase.cpp:51`) = effective maximum PWM.

**Consequences to remember:**
- With setpoint 40 **or** 45, if the wheel does not reach the requested RPM, the PWM to the motor is the SAME (255). **The "boost" 40→45 does NOT add traction.**
- If with PWM 255 the robot still does not climb → the cause is **physical** (torque/traction/weight/geometry/battery). **No firmware change resolves this.**
- This **refutes** "slow PID" (saturates sub-second) as a cause of P1 and makes "boost/pitch" causes **irrelevant** for climbing (even if they are true in code).

# PROBLEM 1 — Does not climb the ramp

## Root causes (ordered by probability of being today's failure)

### CAUSE A — Anti-stall that backs up/bullies on the ramp (candidate #1 from *software*)
**Mechanism VERIFIED-IN-CODE; to trigger on the ramp NEEDS-BANK.**

It is the **only new behavior change** in the hot path of linetrack compared to the repo (differential: the repo does NOT have anti-stall).
- It is called **unconditionally** every loop in case 7: `main.cpp:2115-2120` (`if (chequearAtasco(...)) { recuperarAtasco(); break; }`).
- It triggers if `min(ΔfrontRight, ΔfrontLeft) < 15` pulses/100 ms sustained **for 3 s** (`UMBRAL_RUEDA=15` L1614, `STUCK_TIME_MS=3000` L1616). **Does not read pitch/IMU**: treats the ramp the same as a donkey hill.
- Recalculation: 15 pulses/100 ms = 150 pulses/s ÷ 25 pulses/cm = **6.0 cm/s**. If the slower wheel climbs at <6 cm/s for 3 consecutive seconds → "stall". *(The factor 25 pulses/cm comes from `runDistance`; the `[CAL]` logs raw pulses, so the measurement does not depend on that factor being exact.)*
- The grace of 8 s is set up **only once** at startup (`main.cpp:1850`) and **never re-armed** → on the ramp (which is far from startup) **it has already expired**.
- `recuperarAtasco()` (`main.cpp:1661-1671`): 150 ms of **reverse at speed 90** + **450 ms of advance at speed 100**.

**Correction from July 2:** it does not "only back up". It does a short reverse **and then charges full for 450 ms**. On the ramp, the net effect is a cycle *"back a little / charge"* every ~3 s, which can **help** (momentum) or **push it off the ramp** — which of the two is physical.

Why it is candidate #1 from software: it is 100% code (does not depend on the BNO), it is the only NEW thing in the hot path, and "does not climb" is compatible with "every 3 s it backs up".

### CAUSE B — Mechanical torque/traction limit (global candidate #1)
**NEEDS-BANK. The code neither confirms nor refutes it, but points to it.**
From point 1: the firmware already sends PWM 255 when the wheel brakes. If it does not climb with maximum torque, **it is mechanical** (weight, distribution over the drive axle, rubber, reduction, attack angle, battery tension). It is, by physical frequency, the most common cause of "does not climb the ramp" in Rescue Line.

### CAUSE C (WITHDRAWN) — "steer frozen in case 7"
**REFUTED.** See §0.1: the serial is drained via `yield()` from the I2C readings. The steer is fresh. **No** need to add `serialEvent5()` to case 7.

### CAUSE D — Doubtful slope detection (real in code, but irrelevant for climbing)
`main.cpp:1365` `pitch = event.orientation.y`; threshold `pitch > 3.9` of a single sign, without offset, without hysteresis; `velocidadBase` is dead code (`1377-1385`). **All true**, but from point 1 **correcting it does not add torque** → does not make it climb the ramp. Its only value for P1 is as a *gate* for the anti-stall (Solution A1), and for that, it is necessary to know which axis is the pitch (§0.2, NEEDS-BANK).

### Discarded for P1 (do not waste time)
- **Boost 40→45 / dead `velocidadBase`** (L1-C2/L2-2): true, but cosmetic (point 1). Debt, not fix.
- **Inner wheel in reverse with |steer|>0.7** (`drivebase.cpp:141-146`, `55−2·0.7·55 = −22` RPM): true, but it is the **same** behavior on flat that works today. It would only apply if there is a tight curve **over** the ramp (data nonexistent in code).
- **"twisted steer → inner wheel stuck → triggers anti-stall":** refuted — `chequearAtasco` uses `labs(Δpulsos)` (`main.cpp:1642-1643`); a wheel in reverse has high Δ, does not count as stuck.
- **"pure integral PID leaves torque low":** refuted — saturates to 255 in ~300 ms.

## Solution (the simplest and most reliable): MEASURE before touching

**Do not change a line before Step 0.** Today it is not proven which of A/B is the real mechanism, and B (mechanical) cannot be fixed with firmware. The firmware **already has all the telemetry** — the measurement takes ~10 min and 1 line of temporary print.

**Step 0 — Discriminative measurement (mandatory, almost zero code):**
1. Temporarily add in case 7 (after `main.cpp:2115`):
   `Serial.print("pitch="); Serial.print(pitch); Serial.print(" pwm="); Serial.print(fr.getPWM()); Serial.print(" set="); Serial.println(velocidadAjustada);`
   and for the BNO axis, also log `event.orientation.x/y/z`.
2. Run the robot climbing the real ramp, in linetrack, with the grace already expired (competition condition), with the serial monitor open. `[CAL] frD/flD/min` (`1647-1649`) and `[ATASCO]` (`1663`) are already printed.
3. **Read the result:**
   - **`[ATASCO]` appears during the climb** → **CAUSE A**. Go to A1/A2.
   - **`[ATASCO]` does NOT appear, `pwm ≈ 255` and does not climb** → **CAUSE B (mechanical)**. **Do not touch firmware.**
   - Note which axis (`x/y/z`) changes when tilting and with what sign → resolves §0.2 and enables A1.

**If the bank shows `[ATASCO]` on the ramp:**
- **A1 (the simplest, if the pitch turned out usable) — gate by pitch in `chequearAtasco`** (start, `main.cpp:1619`), replicating the form of the existing grace gate:
  ```cpp
  if (leer_pitch() > UMBRAL_RAMPA) { stuck_since = now; return false; }
  ```
  Use the axis/threshold that confirmed Step 0. Leaves the anti-stall intact for the flat hill; only silences it when tilted. Fails for sure: if the axis is wrong, it does not worsen (remains as today).
- **A2 (if the pitch is not useful) — deactivate the anti-stall only in case 7** via a new flag in `priority_fix_flags.h` (default off) or by commenting `main.cpp:2117-2120`. Returns case 7 to the behavior **of the repo** (which climbed or not without backing up). Cost: loses the anti-stall recovery throughout the run.
- **A3 (patch, less reliable) — increase `STUCK_TIME_MS`** (`1616`) from 3000 to > time to crown. A literal; does not distinguish ramp from hill. Only temporary.

**If the bank shows `pwm ≈ 255` without climbing:** mechanical cause. Firmware does not touch anything. Goes to hardware (weight/rubber/distribution/CG), documented in `hardware/cambios_de_hardware.md`.

# PROBLEM 2 — Does not enter rescue / does not detect silver

## Reconciliation with today's behavior (read first)
**Today's run does NOT test P2.** The silver line marks the entry to evacuation, which in Rescue Line is **after** the ramp. If the robot did not climb the ramp, **it is very likely that it never stepped on the silver tape**. Then:
- That today it "did not enter rescue" is **explained by P1** (did not arrive), not necessarily by the silver bugs.
- The silver detection bugs are **VERIFIED-IN-CODE** (would prevent entry even if it arrived), but **their activation today is INCONCLUSIVE**.
- **Operational priority:** first P1. P2 is closed in the bank **in parallel**, because they are demonstrated bugs; it is not validated on the track until the robot physically reaches the silver.

## Verified root causes

There are **two independent paths** to `action=2 → routine="rescue"`: (A) local APDS sensor (`main.cpp:1974`), (B) `silver_line` via serial from the RPi (`main.cpp:1970`). The subsequent gating is **healthy** (C0).

### C0 — The gating is NOT the barrier (VERIFIED-IN-CODE 100%)
`taskDone` is `true` upon entering the line and **never returns to `false`** (grep: `taskDone=false` does not exist); `if(taskDone)` (`1940`) always runs. `case 2` (`2024`) makes `rutina="rescue"` without extra condition. **One detector is enough.** The failure is 100% upstream: **no detector triggers.** Do not look for the bug in the gating.

### C1 — [Path A / APDS, MAIN] The threshold for "Silver" is unreachable with its own calibration (VERIFIED-IN-CODE)
- Live route: `get_color_fast()` (`1886`) → `classify_color()` (`604`). It is the only live classifier (`get_color_old`/`get_color_blocking_legacy` are dead).
- Threshold (`main.cpp:625`): `if (c > 2220 && ratio_rc > 0.234f) → "Silver"`.
- Calibrated reference for silver (`main.cpp:536`): `{500,900,900,2300}` → **r/c = 500/2300 = 0.2174 < 0.234 ⇒ FAIL** (at c=2300 the threshold requires r ≥ 538; silver measures 500). Falls into the **"White"** branch (`629`: `c>1500 && ratio_rc≤0.235`).
- **Aggravating — the table is physically incoherent:** the White `{570,…,2685}` is **brighter** than silver (c 2685 > 2300) and its r/c=0.2123 is almost identical. I recalculated **all axes**: r/c 0.212 vs 0.217; g/c 0.376 vs 0.391; r/g 0.564 vs 0.556; r/b identical. **No axis in the table separates silver from white.**
- Consequence: `color_detected=="Silver"` is never true → never `plateadoDetectado` (`1893`) → never `action=2` (`1974`) nor `Serial5.write(241)` (`1896`).
- **NEW:** the same broken `classify_color` is also used by `detectarPlateado()` (`1294`) and `procesarColorEvacuacion()` (`1317`) → the bug affects silver detection **also within evacuation**, not just entry.

### C2 — [Path B / serial] The silver by vision is never emitted (VERIFIED-IN-CODE)
- **RPi: mask in the wrong color space.** `Main.py:793` `silver_mask = cv2.inRange(frame_resized, lower_silver_hsv, upper_silver_hsv)`. `frame_resized` is **BGR** (`770`, resize without converting); the limits are HSV (`74-75`). Recalculation: the intersection of bands for a neutral gray (B=G=R) is **empty**; only a dark navy blue matches. **Silver is mathematically impossible to detect.** (Red, on the other hand, does use `hsv_frame`, `789-790`.) → the RPi always sends `silver_line=0`.
- **Correction to an item from July 2 and this audit:** the sub-cause "the Teensy does not drain `silver_line` in case 7" is **FALSE** (§0.1: it drains via `yield()` from I2C). Path B does not die due to the Teensy serial; it dies **in the RPi**, which never sets `silver_line=1`.

### C3 — RPi/Teensy desync (real, but NOT a proximate cause)
The RPi flips `estado='rescue'` locally by its own detection (`Main.py:890-891`) without waiting for the 241, and a trigger from path B does not resend 241. **Verified**, but it is what happens *after* detecting silver. With the detection broken, fixing the desync does not move the needle. **Debt, not fix for P2.**

## Solution (the simplest and most reliable): MEASURE before touching the threshold

**Principle: resolve ONE path reliably, not both halfway.** Path A (APDS) is the shortest and self-sufficient (does not depend on the RPi or the serial). It is the primary fix.

**Step A — APDS Measurement (mandatory, 0 logic changes):**
1. `main.cpp:611` → `bool shouldPrint = true;` (the print is already wired). Flash.
2. With the sensor at **real track height and speed** and competition lighting, log `R, G, B, C, r/c` over: (i) the real silver tape for evacuation, (ii) the white of the track. ~20 samples of each.
3. **Decision:** Does any axis (c, r/c, g/c, …) separate the two clouds with margin?
   - **Yes** → **Step B**: rewrite ONLY the condition `main.cpp:625` with the cut at the measured midpoint. Do not touch anything else in the chain (it is healthy, C0).
   - **No** → the APDS does not discriminate silver from white; go to path B (vision).
4. Revert `shouldPrint=false` before competing.

**Why measuring is mandatory:** the current table gives silver ≈ white on all axes, and the silver reference is **suspected of being stale** (a specular surface should give C **higher** than matte white; the table says otherwise). **Lowering the 0.234 blindly could trigger false rescue over white in the middle of the track — worse than today.** Recommending a number without a bank is guessing.

**Fix for path B (redundancy, or primary if the APDS does not separate) — `Main.py:793`, 1 word:**
```python
silver_mask = cv2.inRange(hsv_frame, lower_silver_hsv, upper_silver_hsv)
```
`hsv_frame` is already computed (`785`), reuses the HSV calibration, and remains coherent with red. Eliminates the mathematical impossibility. **But** requires recalibrating `lower/upper_silver_hsv` (`74-75`) over the real tape with `calibration.py` under competition light; without that, it eliminates the bug but does not guarantee detection. (Does not need to touch the Teensy serial: it is already drained.)

**Architectural decision:** choose **one** source of truth. If the bank shows that the APDS separates silver from white → APDS primary, path B remains as optional debt. If it does not separate → vision is the source (fix RPi + recalibration). **Do not fix both halfway.**

## What is CONFIRMED / DISCARDED / is NEW compared to July 2

**Confirmed (recalculated from zero):** anti-stall without gate by pitch inserted in the hot path; grace of 8 s that has already expired on the ramp; cosmetic boost + dead `velocidadBase`; incoherent APDS threshold (silver → "White"); RPi `inRange` BGR with HSV limits.

**Discarded / corrected:**
- **"Serial/steer frozen on line"** → refuted (I2C does `yield()` → drains serial). Applies to P1 (was not the cause) and to P2 (path B does not die due to the Teensy serial).
- **"Slow PID leaves torque low"** → refuted (saturates to 255 in ~300 ms).
- **"Fixing pitch/boost makes it climb the ramp"** → discarded (PWM already saturated).
- **"Twisted steer triggers the anti-stall"** → refuted (`labs`).
- **"Just lower the threshold 0.234 and it works"** → discarded as certainty: the table does not separate silver from white on any axis; without a bank, it is guessing and could worsen.
- **Axis `.y` = roll** → not verifiable by code (contradictory sources); NEEDS-BANK.

**New:**
- **`PID::Reset()` is never called** → free integrator → PWM saturates to 255 → reorders everything P1 (mechanical vs software).
- **The anti-stall is NEW code** (differential vs repo): the only behavior change in the hot path.
- **`taskDone` never returns to `false`** → gating is not the barrier (P2).
- **The topology** (silver after the ramp) → today’s behavior does not test P2.
- The same broken `classify_color` also affects silver detection **in evacuation**.

4. **P2 · Step A** (APDS measurement silver vs white; only enable the print). In parallel with P1. No risk.
5. **P2 · fix according to bank:** rewrite the cut in `main.cpp:625` (only touches the White/Silver boundary; does not touch Black/Green/Red/motors/PID/comms), or switch to vision (`Main.py:793` + recalibrate).
6. **Do not touch:** gating (C0), chain after classification, serial protocol (C3), and all validated subsystems. No redesigns (hysteresis/fusion/handshake) until the bank shows that the minimum fix does not reach.

**Hard rule:** no threshold or control firmware changes reach the students without prior bank measurement. Hardware testing is closed by the human team.
